sections.h2: Where does a Pitt County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
A deed for Pitt County land is recorded at the Pitt County Register of Deeds, at 100 E. 1st Street in Greenville. Per the county page, the doors open at 8:00 and close at 5:00 on weekdays, and the phone is 252-902-1650.

The same office keeps deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and the other land papers that make up the chain of title. Some of the records go back to the 1700s, since Pitt County was formed in 1760. For a seller, the office matters at one moment above all: the deed that moves the house to a buyer has to land in these books before it protects anyone.

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter when selling a Pitt County house?
sections.html:
Because the first paper on file wins. Under G.S. 47-18, a deed, option or lease longer than three years carries no weight against lien creditors or paying purchasers until it is filed in the land's home county, and ranking is set by filing time.

Greenville is where that time stamp gets set, which is why every closing ends with a filing step. A signed deed left in a drawer protects nobody. Hold an old deed from a family transfer that never reached the office? File it, or talk to an attorney, before you advertise the house.

sections.h2: What will Pitt County charge to file a deed?
sections.html:
The General Assembly sets the fees, and the county page says they match in all 100 counties. The Pitt summary lists these items:

  • General instruments such as deeds and easements: $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each extra page.
  • Plats: $21 per sheet.
  • Non-standard document: $25 added to the base fee.
  • Several instruments filed together: $10 for each additional one.
  • Certified copy of a recorded document: $5 for the first page and $2 for each extra page.
  • Satisfaction or cancellation of a mortgage or deed of trust: no charge.

The county's summary lists mortgages and deeds of trust at $56 for the first 15 pages, while the current text of G.S. 161-10 prints $64 for the first 35 pages. Call before sending a lender document so the check matches. The office takes cash, checks, money orders and major cards.

sections.h2: How is the Pitt County deed stamp tax figured?
sections.html:
The excise tax runs a dollar for every $500 of price, with a leftover part of $500 counting as a full one. Pitt's records page says it follows the sale price and is paid at filing.

The seller carries the duty, according to G.S. 105-228.30, and it must reach the register before the deed is accepted. The proceeds split evenly between the county and the State. Look for the line on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: Does Pitt County accept electronic filing?
sections.html:
Yes. The county takes electronic filings through several vendors and tells filers to call each one to compare prices. The vendors named on the county page are Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Indecomm Global Services and Simplifile.

Most sellers never touch this step, since the settlement office sends the deed and the buyer's loan papers together. A family transfer with no lender is different: ask whoever prepared the deed whether they file electronically or in person, and who covers the vendor charge.

sections.h2: How can a Pitt County owner watch for deed fraud and check records?
sections.html:
Pitt County has an alert sign-up that notifies owners whenever a filing matches their name or property. The county also runs an online search for recorded documents from September 1762 to the present, searchable by grantor, grantee, document type, book and page, or date range.

  • Search the grantor index for your name to see every recorded deed or lien tied to you.
  • Use book and page numbers from an old deed to pull the full document.
  • Use the county's Online Parcel Information System, run by Tax Administration and GIS, to view parcel boundaries, assessed values, tax districts and flood zones.
  • Older index books can be used on site at the Greenville office.

Do this before listing, especially with an inherited house. A loan that was never released, or a gap in the chain of title, is far easier to fix before a buyer is waiting.

sections.h2: What other papers might a Pitt County sale involve?
sections.html:
Beyond the deed, a Pitt County closing can include a deed of trust for the buyer's loan, a recorded release of the seller's old loan, and sometimes a plat or easement. Each one is filed separately and priced under the fee list above.

  • Old loan: confirm the lender recorded a satisfaction.
  • New loan: the buyer's lender records its own deed of trust.
  • Seller financing: see the contract for deed rules in Chapter 47H, which call for recording within five business days.

The county's FAQ lists agreements, assignments, assumed names, leases and subdivision maps among the land-related documents the office records.

sections.h2: What should a Pitt County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Begin with a title check. Pull the deed that put the house in your name, confirm each old loan has a filed release, and ask the tax office what is owed.

Property tax lives in a different office. Under G.S. 105-360, a bill is due September 1 and starts collecting interest after January 5. Pitt County Tax Administration, not this page, gives the balance on your parcel.

A house that needs repairs, has tenants or sits in an estate can still sell to a direct cash buyer on a short timeline. The filing steps stay the same: the deed goes to Greenville.

faqs.q: Where is the Pitt County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 100 E. 1st Street, Greenville, NC 27834. The county page shows weekday hours from 8:00 to 5:00 and the number 252-902-1650.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamp tax in a Pitt County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. G.S. 105-228.30 names the transferor, and the office collects the tax when the deed is filed. Your settlement statement should show the line.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to file a mortgage release in Pitt County?
faqs.a: No. The county lists satisfactions and cancellations as free. The lender is the one that files the release, so ask yours to do it.

faqs.q: Is there an online deed search for Pitt County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says documents recorded from September 1762 forward can be searched online by name, type, book and page, or dates.

faqs.q: What is the base fee for a Pitt County deed?
faqs.a: $26 covers the first 15 pages of a general instrument, then $4 for each page past that. Plats are $21 a sheet. Ask the office for the total on your document, including any non-standard format charge.
